paragraphs: Rav Yitzchak bar Chinena or Chanina.

He was a disciple of Rav Huna. In [Ketubot 4b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.4b.3): “Rabbi Yitzchak bar Ch. said: Rav Huna said.” In Ketubot 61b, “R' Yitzchak bar Chanina said: Rav Huna said” occurs three times. [Berakhot 52b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.52b.22) has “Rabbi Yosi son of R' Chanina said: Rav Huna said”; this should read R' Yitzchak bar Ch., as in the Rif and Dikdukei Soferim there, note yod. [Nedarim 38b](https://www.sefaria.org/Nedarim.38b.2) has Rav Yitzchak bar Chanania saying “Rav Huna said.” [Sanhedrin 38b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.38b.2) has Rabbi Yochanan son of R' Chanina; Seder HaDorot suggests that it should perhaps read R' Yitzchak bar Ch., while Dikdukei Soferim there reads R' Chama bar Ch.[^1]

notes.text: Chinena and Chanina represent Hyman’s two heading forms. Where he abbreviates the patronymic ב״ח or בר״ח, “bar Ch.” retains that abbreviation. His definite correction in Berakhot differs from Seder HaDorot’s “perhaps” in Sanhedrin. The Rif and Dikdukei Soferim readings are cited as Hyman reports them; “note yod” is the lettered note.

The Davidson text calls him Rabbi Yitzchak at Ketubot 4b:3, but Rav Yitzchak at Nedarim 38b:2. Berakhot has Rabbi Yosi bar Chanina, while Sanhedrin has Rabbi Yochanan bar Chanina; Hyman discusses competing readings of these names.
